text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate on hosted API (region: eu). 5xx rate = 5.0% over last 5m, affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/embed. Dash: https://dash.internal/redwood/alerts/1820001111
Sara G.: Oncall here — just saw the page. I'm pulling logs & checking runtime pools. Paging SRE rotation.
Sara G.: Quick read: runtime-prod-eu-2 queue depth spiked, p99 latency >2s, upstream RPC timeouts increasing. Likely queueing/backpressure rather than model OOM.
Raj P.: If it's queueing we should reduce max_inflight and enable shedding for lower-priority work. Can we route guest/anonymous traffic to a degraded pool or throttle at the edge?
Sara G.: I'm going to apply an emergency rate limit for guest-plan and reduce max_inflight on the pool. Starting with edge throttle.
Sara G.: Running:
```
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/ratelimits" \ 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_OPS_TOKEN" \ 
 -d '{"selector":"plan:guest","limit_per_s":5,"reason":"emergency-mitigation 1820001111"}'
```
ops-bot: rate limit change accepted and propagated to edge nodes.
Liz (support): Which customers are hitting this? We have ticket #4298 reporting 502s from AcmeMaps and #4301 from Shoply.
Sara G.: Noted. Also lowering runtime pool config now: reduce max_inflight from 1000 -> 250, set request timeout 20s, enable fast shedding for embed/generation low priority.
Sara G.: Applying runtime change:
```
# runtimectl
set-pool-config --pool runtime-prod-eu-2 --max-inflight 250 --request-timeout 20s --shedding-mode fast
```
runbook-bot: Runbook excerpt: backpressure mitigation — reduce pool max_inflight, enable shedding, shorten request timeout, apply per-plan edge throttles, and optionally disable non-essential tooling. See /runbooks/backpressure for post-incident updates.
Kevin M.: Rolling the change. Watching queue length and 5xx.
ops-bot: runtime-prod-eu-2 config applied. Pool is draining gracefully; new connections limited to 250 in-flight.
ops-bot: Observed queue length down ~70% within 3m.
Sara G.: 5xx rate dropped from 5.0% -> 0.8% over 6m. p95 latency back to expected range. Good signal.
Sara G.: Keeping guest-plan throttle at 5r/s for 30m, then we'll do a gradual raise. I'll notify support & sales about affected customers.
Raj P.: Recommend: create temporary quota exceptions for enterprise customers who hit the throttle and need higher QPS (so they don't get impacted by guest-level throttles). Schedule postmortem + thresholds review.
Liz (support): Contacting AcmeMaps and Shoply now, updating tickets #4298 #4301 with mitigation steps and ETA.
Sara G.: Handoff: I'm off in 10. Raj — taking the night pager? Summary: edge rate limit guest->5r/s, pool runtime-prod-eu-2 max_inflight->250, request-timeout->20s, shedding=fast. Current state: degraded -> recovering.
Raj P.: Ack, taking over. I'll keep throttles for 45m and then test incremental raises while monitoring errors. Creating incident record INC-2026.
support-bot: Created incident INC-2026 and linked support tickets #4298, #4301.
Sara G.: Also toggled a non-essential tooling flag to reduce background load while this stabilizes.
Raj P.: Command used: 
```
/ops/flags set disable-llm-tooling=true --until "2026-03-15T02:00Z" --reason "mitigation 1820001111"
```
Kevin M.: :thumbsup: Nice quick triage. Please add timeline & config diffs to the incident doc so we can include in the postmortem.
Sara G.: Will add details. Also propose a follow-up change: make edge throttles dynamic by pool load and add an automated short-circuit for embeddings when queue depth > N.
Raj P.: Agreed. I'll keep monitoring through the night, and we'll aim to reopen the runbook with clearer thresholds.
Sara G.: Thanks everyone. Leaving notes in INC-2026 and will add runbook updates tomorrow.
